info.title: HR Assessment Platform
info.description: Every operation declares `x-roles` (who may call it) and `x-required-flag` (the feature flag that must be on for the organization; `null` when ungated). Public operations have `x-roles: []` and no security requirement. Errors use one envelope: `{error: {code, message_key, details, request_id}}`. Response examples without a hand-written one are generated from the response model.

get.description: Returns `ok` while the process is running. It does not touch the database; use it for container liveness probes.
Opens a database connection and runs `SELECT 1`. Returns 503 while the database is unreachable, so load balancers stop sending traffic.
Product slug, build version and runtime environment (`dev`, `test` or `prod`).
Prometheus text format: HTTP requests, AI calls, exam starts and audit events of this API process. Super admin only (bearer token); not exposed to organizations.

get.summary: Download an object through a short-lived signed token
get.description: The token is the authorization: it is issued only after the caller passed the owning module's own access check and audit entry, and it expires after about a minute. Images and PDFs are served inline, everything else as an attachment. Encrypted snapshots are decrypted server-side. An invalid or expired token is `NOT_FOUND`.

200.description: The object bytes with its content type.

404.description: NOT_FOUND: bad signature, malformed or expired token.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password
post.description: Constant-time credential check with a generic `INVALID_CREDENTIALS` for an unknown email or a wrong password. Five consecutive failures lock the account for 15 minutes (`ACCOUNT_LOCKED`). On success the access token is returned in the body and the rotating refresh token is set as an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie. If the user has an authenticator app, `totp_required` is true, no token is issued, and the client completes the login at `/auth/login/totp` with `totp_token`. `must_change_password` true means only `/auth/change-password`, `/auth/me` and `/auth/logout` work.

post.summary: Complete a sign-in with the authenticator code
post.description: Second step after `/auth/login` or `/auth/google` returned `totp_required`. Accepts the 6-digit code or a single-use recovery code. Wrong codes count toward the same lockout as wrong passwords. The challenge `totp_token` expires after 5 minutes.

post.summary: Sign in with a Google ID token
post.description: The server verifies the ID token and requires a verified email that belongs to an existing, active user whose email domain is in the organization's allowed Google domains. There is no auto-provisioning. An organization with an empty allowed list has Google sign-in switched off. Response and cookie are the same as `/auth/login`.

post.summary: Rotate the refresh token and get a new access token
post.description: Reads the refresh cookie, issues a new access token and replaces the cookie. Every refresh token works once: presenting an already-rotated token revokes the whole token family (the session ends everywhere it was copied). A session idle for longer than the organization's timeout (default 30 minutes) cannot be refreshed. Failures clear the cookie.

post.description: Revokes the refresh-token family of the calling session and clears the cookie. Allowed while a forced password change is pending. The access token stays valid until it expires (15 minutes); use `/auth/logout-all` to kill every token immediately.
Bumps the user's token version, which invalidates every access token at once, and revokes all refresh tokens.

Required on first login and after a temporary password was issued. Checks the current password, the organization's password policy (minimum length, common-password blocklist) and that none of the last 5 passwords is reused (`PASSWORD_POLICY_FAILED`, `details.violations`). Success bumps the token version (all old tokens die) and returns a fresh session so the user stays signed in. The default super admin password is protected (`PROTECTED_ACCOUNT`).
Generates a secret for the calling admin. It stays pending until `/auth/totp/verify` confirms a code. Calling it again before verifying replaces the pending secret.
Checks a code from the app, turns the second factor on and returns recovery codes once.
Needs the current password and a valid code (or a recovery code). Blocked with `FORBIDDEN` (`details.reason = totp_required_by_org`) for an org admin whose organization requires TOTP.

get.description: The organization's identity provider setup. The client secret is never returned, only `has_secret`. `redirect_uri` is read-only: paste it into the identity provider. `status` is `not_set_up`, `needs_test`, `disabled` or `active`.

put.description: Provider (`google`, `microsoft` with `tenant_id`, or `oidc` with `issuer`), client id, write-only client secret (omit to keep; required the first time), scopes, allowed email domains (lowercased, unique across organizations: `VALIDATION_ERROR` with `domain_taken`), `enabled` and `sso_required`. Changing the connection (provider, issuer, tenant, client id, secret, scopes or domains) resets the verified state. `enabled` and `sso_required` need a verified provider (`SSO_NOT_VERIFIED`). Audited as `SSO_CONFIG_UPDATED`.

delete.description: Deletes the provider, its domains and the linked identities. Password login is unaffected.

post.description: Returns the `authorize_url` for the calling admin's own test sign-in and sets the signed state cookie. When the admin's email passes every check the callback marks the provider verified (`SSO_TESTED`) and redirects to `{APP_BASE_URL}/settings/sign-in?sso_test=ok` (or `=failed`). The admin's email domain must be in the domain list. Rate limited.

post.summary: Does this email sign in with SSO?
post.description: Answers by email domain only (never by user lookup, so it does not reveal whether an address exists). `sso` is true when the domain's organization has an enabled, tested provider. `sso_required` is the organization switch: non-admin users are refused at password login, organization admins keep it, so the login page should keep a small password link. Rate limited.

Creates `state`, `nonce` and the PKCE verifier, keeps them in a signed 10 minute HttpOnly cookie (SameSite=Lax, nothing stored server-side) and returns the identity provider's `authorize_url`; the browser navigates there. `SSO_NOT_CONFIGURED` when the domain has no usable provider. Rate limited.

get.description: Where the identity provider sends the browser back. Checks state and cookie, exchanges the code (client secret and PKCE), validates the ID token, then finds the existing active user in the organization that owns the provider. Always answers `303`: success sets the refresh cookie and goes to `{APP_BASE_URL}/sso/done` (the client then calls `POST /auth/refresh`); an enabled authenticator app goes to `{APP_BASE_URL}/login/totp#totp_token=...`; any failure goes to `{APP_BASE_URL}/login?sso_error=failed|expired|unavailable` (generic on purpose; the reason is audited). Rate limited.

bearerAuth.description: Staff access token (audience `api`) from `POST /api/v1/auth/login`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Lives 15 minutes; renew with `POST /api/v1/auth/refresh`.

examSession.description: Candidate exam session token (audience `exam`) from `POST /api/v1/exam/session/open`, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Valid for at most 12 hours.

examBindingCookie.name: exam_binding
examBindingCookie.description: HttpOnly browser-binding cookie set by `POST /api/v1/exam/session/open`. Exam routes refuse a token that arrives without it (`LINK_BOUND_TO_OTHER_SESSION`).
